thread-s1.subject: Onboarding schedule for Marcus
thread-s1.snippet: Confirming the onboarding sessions for the first two weeks of August.

messages.snippet: Confirming the onboarding sessions for the first two weeks of August.
messages.body:
Hi Marcus,

Thank you for sending the account details yesterday. I am confirming the onboarding sessions for the first two weeks of August.

1. Data import walkthrough, Tuesday 5 August, one hour.
2. Admin and permissions setup, Thursday 7 August, 45 minutes.
3. Reporting review, Tuesday 12 August, one hour.

If any of those times do not work, tell me which and I will move them. I will send calendar invitations once you confirm.

Best,
Alex Reyes

thread-s2.subject: Follow-up on the integration questions
thread-s2.snippet: Answers to the three questions from our call, plus one open item.

messages.snippet: Answers to the three questions from our call, plus one open item.
messages.body:
Hi Marcus,

Here are the answers to the three questions from our call on Tuesday.

1. Yes, the API supports incremental sync and we recommend it for volumes above 50,000 records.
2. Retention is configurable per environment, and 90 days is the default.
3. Single sign-on is included at your tier, with no additional cost.

The one open item is the sandbox credential request, which is with our security team. I expect it back by Friday and will let you know either way.

Best,
Alex Reyes

thread-s3.subject: Revised timeline
thread-s3.snippet: The revised timeline moves go-live to 22 September.

messages.snippet: The revised timeline moves go-live to 22 September.
messages.body:
Hi Marcus,

After reviewing the scope with my team, the revised timeline moves go-live to 22 September. The two-week shift comes entirely from the data migration, which is larger than the estimate we worked from in May.

Everything else in the plan is unchanged, and the training dates hold. I am sorry for the change and I would rather give you an accurate date now than a comfortable one today.

Best,
Alex Reyes

thread-s13.subject: Search latency: fixed
thread-s13.snippet: Search latency is back under 200ms as of this morning.

messages.snippet: Search latency is back under 200ms as of this morning.
messages.body:
Priya,

Search latency is back under 200ms as of this morning. No customer escalations came in overnight.

- Root cause was an unbounded cache key, fixed in build 412.
- We are adding an alert on key cardinality this week.
- I will fold the write-up into Thursday's review.

Nothing needed from you.

Alex

thread-s16.subject: Incident summary: export outage
thread-s16.snippet: Exports were down for 51 minutes yesterday. Cause and fix below.

messages.snippet: Exports were down for 51 minutes yesterday. Cause and fix below.
messages.body:
Priya,

Exports were down for 51 minutes yesterday afternoon.

- Cause was a bad migration that locked the jobs table.
- We restored from the standby and reran the failed exports overnight.
- Two customers noticed and both have been contacted.

Full write-up goes out Friday.

Alex
